answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether it sells dune maps, canyon surveys, or walnut harvest forecasts. Creating new keys is free, but activating 10,000 fake agents ties up $1 million for a month. The bond does not prove identities are unique; it makes a swarm consume capital in direct proportion to its size, imposing financing costs even if every bond is later returned.
